title: WMI Subscription
overview: Inspect a permanent WMI subscription binding and compare the owner and change context.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A new permanent WMI binding with unknown ownership warrants a review of the filter, consumer and registration actor.
evidence: Use Sysmon 21 to link filter and consumer. Check related filter and consumer records and authorized endpoint management changes.
false_positive: Managed inventory software can register subscriptions during onboarding.
tuning: Review specific inventory consumer names and signed owner identities before adding an exception.
response: Preserve filter, consumer, binding and process telemetry. Remove confirmed unauthorized registrations with endpoint approval.
prevention: Collect WMI activity and monitor changes to permanent subscriptions on high-value hosts.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture models binding telemetry only. It contains no command or registration code.

questions.explanation: The binding shows the link that requires review.

questions.prompt: What do you check before removal?
options: The order of log display columns
Consumer ownership and authorized management changes
questions.explanation: Endpoint software may use legitimate permanent subscriptions.
